title: Directions and regions
subtitle: Talking about parts of a country
explanation: Use le nord, le sud, l’est, and l’ouest to talk about north, south, east, and west.

title: Question words
subtitle: Asking basic questions
explanation: French question words usually come at the start of the question. Course 12 uses que, où, quand, qui, comment, pourquoi, and combien.

title: Où
subtitle: Asking where
explanation: Use où to ask where something is or where someone can go.

title: Que
subtitle: Asking what
explanation: Use que before a verb to ask what. It appears in questions like “what are you eating?” and “what do you want?”.

examples.eng: What do you want to eat?
What did you want to eat?

title: Comment
subtitle: Asking how
explanation: Use comment to ask how. It can also appear in questions asking someone’s name.

title: Pourquoi
subtitle: Asking why
explanation: Use pourquoi to ask why something happens or why someone did something.

examples.eng: Why was he scared of her?
Why is he washing his feet?

title: Combien
subtitle: How much / how many
explanation: Use combien to ask how much or how many. Add de before the thing being counted.

examples.eng: How many shoes do you have?
How much is it for three weeks?

title: Combien de temps
subtitle: Asking how long
explanation: Use combien de temps to ask how long or for how long.

examples.eng: How long are you here for?
examples.fre: Pour combien de temps es-tu ici?

examples.eng: How long did they work here?
examples.fre: Pour combien de temps ont-ils travaillé ici?

title: À quelle heure
subtitle: Asking at what time
explanation: Use à quelle heure to ask at what time something happens.

examples.eng: What time are you going to the beach?
examples.fre: À quelle heure vas-tu / allez-vous à la plage?

examples.eng: What time are you getting up?

title: Puis-je
subtitle: Asking may I / can I
explanation: Use puis-je to politely ask “can I” or “may I”. It is followed by an infinitive verb.

title: Pouvez-vous
subtitle: Asking can you
explanation: Use pouvez-vous to politely ask another person if they can do something.

examples.eng: Can you tell me the date?
Can you tell me when the film starts?
examples.fre: Peux-tu me dire quand le film commence?

title: Voulez-vous
subtitle: Asking do you want
explanation: Use voulez-vous before an infinitive to ask what someone wants to do.

examples.eng: What do you want to eat?
Do you want that for your birthday?

title: Aller + infinitive
subtitle: Going to do something
explanation: Use aller plus an infinitive to say someone is going to do something.

examples.eng: What are you going to order?
I'm going to Paris at seven o'clock.
examples.fre: Je vais à Paris à sept heures.

title: Devoir + infinitive
subtitle: Having to do something
explanation: Use devoir before another verb to say must or have to.

examples.eng: Whom do we have to go with?

title: Infinitives
subtitle: Base form of verbs
explanation: An infinitive is the base form of a verb, like manger, boire, aller, and prendre. It often follows can, want, going to, or have to.

title: Present tense inversion
subtitle: Verb before subject in questions
explanation: French can ask questions by putting the verb before the subject with a hyphen.

title: Est-ce que questions
subtitle: Simple question starter
explanation: Use est-ce que before a normal sentence to turn it into a question.

examples.fre: Est-ce que Marie sait parler anglais?
Où est-ce que nous mangeons ce soir?

title: Qu'est-ce que
subtitle: Asking what before a full sentence
explanation: Use qu’est-ce que when what is followed by a full subject and verb.

examples.eng: What are you going to order?
What do you want to do tomorrow?
examples.fre: Qu'est-ce que tu veux / vous voulez faire demain?

title: Quel / quelle / quels / quelles
subtitle: Asking which
explanation: Use quel forms to ask which. The form changes with masculine, feminine, singular, and plural nouns.

title: À / au for places
subtitle: Saying to or at a place
explanation: Use à before cities and au before masculine places like au restaurant.

title: Chez
subtitle: At someone’s place
explanation: Use chez to say at/to someone’s house or professional place.

examples.eng: would like to go to Pierre's house.
I'm going to Pierre's house at 12 o'clock.
examples.fre: Je vais chez Pierre à douze heures.

examples.eng: Are you coming to my house tomorrow?

title: De for possession
subtitle: Saying of / belonging to
explanation: French often uses de to show possession, where English might use apostrophe-s.

examples.fre: De quelle couleur est la voiture de Pierre?
De quelle couleur est la maison de Marie?

examples.eng: What is Marie's date of birth?
examples.fre: Quelle est la date de naissance de Marie?

title: Avec qui
subtitle: Asking with whom
explanation: Use avec qui to ask who someone is with or did something with.

examples.eng: Whom are they going to speak with?

title: Avec quoi
subtitle: Asking with what
explanation: Use avec quoi to ask what tool, item, or thing was used.

examples.eng: What did they make that with?
What did they fix the car with?
examples.fre: Avec quoi ont-ils réparé la voiture?

title: De quelle couleur
subtitle: Asking what colour
explanation: Use de quelle couleur to ask what colour something is.

examples.fre: De quelle couleur est la voiture?
De quelle couleur sont mes yeux?

title: Time expressions
subtitle: Talking about when
explanation: Words like demain, aujourd’hui, ce soir, maintenant, and plus tard tell when something happens.

title: Passé composé with avoir
subtitle: Talking about completed actions
explanation: Use avoir plus a past participle to say what someone did or has done.

examples.eng: Did they speak a lot of French?

title: Passé composé with être
subtitle: Motion and reflexive completed actions
explanation: Some verbs use être in the passé composé, especially movement and reflexive verbs.

examples.eng: Did you see whom he left with?
examples.fre: Avez-vous vu avec qui il est parti?

examples.eng: Whom did you go to the théâtre with?
examples.fre: Avec qui es-tu / êtes-vous allé au théâtre?

examples.eng: Why didn’t you have a shower earlier?
examples.fre: Pourquoi ne t'es-tu pas douché plus tôt?

title: Past tense questions
subtitle: Asking what happened
explanation: Course 12 uses inversion and question words with past-tense forms like avez-vous, ont-ils, and a-t-il.

examples.eng: Have you had the car washed?
What did they make that with?
Were there any bottles of champagne?
examples.fre: Y avait-il des bouteilles de champagne?

title: Reflexive verbs
subtitle: Actions done to oneself
explanation: Reflexive verbs use me, te, se, nous, or vous. They are common with washing, getting up, and going to bed.

examples.eng: What time are you getting up?
Why is he washing his feet?
Why didn’t you have a shower earlier?
examples.fre: Pourquoi ne t'es-tu pas douché plus tôt?

title: Faire + infinitive
subtitle: Having something done
explanation: Use faire plus an infinitive to say that someone has something done, like having a car washed.

examples.eng: Have you had the car washed?
They haven't had the car washed.
examples.fre: Ils n'ont pas fait laver la voiture.

examples.eng: What did he make that with?

title: Il y avait / y avait-il
subtitle: There was / were
explanation: Use il y avait to say there was or there were. In a question, y avait-il asks was there or were there.

examples.eng: Were there any bottles of champagne?
examples.fre: Y avait-il des bouteilles de champagne?
Il n’y avait pas beaucoup de nourriture.

examples.eng: The shop was open but there was no milk.
examples.fre: Le magasin était ouvert mais il n’y avait pas de lait.

title: Demonstratives
subtitle: This / that before nouns
explanation: French uses ce, cet, cette, and ces to point to this or that noun.

examples.fre: De quelle couleur est cette bouteille?

title: Possessive adjectives
subtitle: My, your, his, her
explanation: Words like mon, ma, mes, votre, and vos show ownership and match the French noun.

examples.fre: De quelle couleur est votre maison?
De quelle couleur sont mes yeux?

examples.eng: Yes, it is for me, thank you.

title: Object pronouns
subtitle: Small words before the verb
explanation: French often places small object words like me, te, t’, and vous before the verb.

examples.fre: Avec quoi puis-je t'aider / vous aider?

examples.eng: Can you tell me when the film starts?
examples.fre: Peux-tu me dire quand le film commence?

examples.eng: Can you tell me the date?

title: Savoir and indirect questions
subtitle: Knowing what / where / when
explanation: Use savoir with question words to say know what, know where, or know when.

examples.eng: Do you know what they want to eat?
examples.fre: Sais-tu / Savez-vous ce qu'ils veulent manger?

examples.eng: Do you know what she thinks?
Can you tell me when the film starts?
examples.fre: Peux-tu me dire quand le film commence?

title: Birthdays and dates
subtitle: Talking about dates
explanation: Course 12 uses dates, birthdays, and date of birth questions.

title: Imperfect tense
subtitle: Background past descriptions
explanation: Use the imperfect for background states or repeated past situations, such as was, were, or used to.

examples.eng: Why was he scared of her?

examples.fre: De quelle couleur était la voiture?

examples.eng: The shop was open but there was no milk.
examples.fre: Le magasin était ouvert mais il n’y avait pas de lait.

title: Negative sentences
subtitle: Saying not
explanation: French commonly uses ne and pas around the verb to make a sentence negative.

examples.eng: The shop was open but there was no milk.
examples.fre: Le magasin était ouvert mais il n’y avait pas de lait.
